conditions: x is any finite real number; trigonometric arguments are in radians and ln is the real logarithm.
The integrand is defined and smooth on the whole real axis because 2+cos(x)>=1. An explicit exact antiderivative is required everywhere, up to one global additive constant.
The substitution cos(x) is not globally injective and has stationary points at every integer multiple of pi. These points are included in the required primitive's differentiability domain.
x is real with x>=1, the entire real domain of the original integrand. ln is the real logarithm and sqrt is the nonnegative real square root.

An explicit exact antiderivative is required on (1,infinity), with a continuous extension to x=1 whose right derivative equals the integrand value zero. A two-sided real derivative at this domain endpoint is not required or defined by the given expression.
The integrand is defined and continuous at x=1. The singular derivative of the substitution sqrt(ln(x)) at one must not create a new exclusion in the returned primitive.
